newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama's cocaine seizures rose 15 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Panama's cocaine seizures rose 15 pct in 1996.

text.p: Panamanian authorities seized more than 8 tons of cocaine last year, 15 percent up on 1995, the head of the police anti-narcotics unit said.

Rosendo Miranda attributed the increase to more cooperation among customs, police anti-drug units and maritime officials since former strongman Manuel Antonio Noriega was toppled in a 1989 U.S. invasion. Noriega is serving a 40-year sentence in a Florida prison on drug and racketeering charges.
"Before there were no morals. There were officials who tried to figure out how they could get a bribe," Miranda told foreign correspondents on Tuesday night.
Marijuana seizures rose 5,600 percent to more than 18 tons in 1996.
Miranda said the figures showed that Panama, because of its location, remained a major transit point for drugs.
"More than 94 percent of drugs seized were going elsewhere, primarily the United States and Europe," he said.
